findings.section: Behaviour contract / C2 (the command's name); Executive summary C2; Decided here (C2 excludes the command's own name)
findings.summary: A command name holding a $ that is not its first character is neither refused nor expanded, so `g$X push origin` and `/usr/bin/$X push origin` are allowed today and stay allowed after B35. This is the same hole C2 closes for arguments. The brief also says a name holding $ is refused 'as one holding $ is today'. Today only a name that starts with $ is refused.
findings.evidence: internal/fence/judge.go, words(): `if strings.HasPrefix(w, "$")` is the only $ check on the command word, and baseName strips the path before match. Built from ee4adf63: `vloop fence check --root <tmp> --phase review --tool bash 'g$X push origin'` prints allow (exit 0), as do '/usr/bin/$X push origin' and 'gi"$X" push'. C2 refuses only a name holding a glob or a brace, and 'Decided here' excludes the name from C2, so all three stay allowed after B35. With X=it, X=git or X=t, each runs git push.
findings.fix: In C2, refuse a command word that is expanded in any way: a $ unquoted or in double quotes anywhere in it, a glob or a brace expansion. Check the whole word, before baseName, so /usr/bin/$X is caught. The message is `command word <word> expands and cannot be judged`; a word starting with $ keeps today's message. Correct the executive summary's 'as one holding $ is today'. Add `review  g$X push origin   → deny: command word g$X expands and cannot be judged` and `review  /usr/bin/$X push origin   → deny: command word /usr/bin/$X expands and cannot be judged` to the worked example, and 'a command name that expands, judged as written' to the violations.

findings.section: Behaviour contract / C2 (definition of a brace expansion)
findings.summary: 'An unquoted { followed later in the word by an unquoted }, with an unquoted , or .. between them' can be read as any { and any later }. On that reading `git log HEAD@{1}..HEAD@{0}` is a brace expansion. It becomes `git log *`, and `Bash(git log*--output*)` denies it. Bash does not expand that word. A gate written to either reading would pass, and the reviews could disagree.
findings.evidence: `bash -c 'echo HEAD@{1}..HEAD@{0}'` prints HEAD@{1}..HEAD@{0}. `echo x{a,b}` prints xa xb. The worked example pins only `git log @{u}..HEAD`, where the .. is outside the braces, so it does not tell the readings apart.
findings.fix: Write it as 'a { and the } that closes it, with an unquoted , or .. directly between them (not inside a nested pair)'. Add `review  git log HEAD@{1}..HEAD@{0}   → allow` to the worked example.

decisions: Drop leading keywords and judge the rest rather than parse the shell grammar (no mvdan.cc/sh): sound. Every command inside is judged, and nothing is judged less than one per line.
case, select, function, coproc and [[ stay refused: sound. None of them is among the counted denials, and case's ) cannot be split safely.

An expanded word stands for any text, including several words, instead of being resolved. It knowingly denies harmless forms such as `git diff "$BASE" --stat` and `vloop task show "$id"` where a fence denies `vloop task done:*`. I agree, because a denial costs only a retry.

A word a wrapper skips that is expanded refuses the whole command (`nice -n $N …`, `env A=$X …`). This tightens today's behaviour: harmless forms like `env PATH="$PATH:x" go test` are now refused. I agree.
command -v and -V (with -p) run nothing and are allowed whatever follows; only the literal option counts: sound, since POSIX command -v does not run the name.
Subshells are read; $(, <( and >( stay refused: sound.
A keyword after a wrapper is not dropped (`env ! x` stays denied): sound and conservative.
A redirection target holding a glob is judged as written, as today. This is the one expansion C2 leaves open; it is low risk because only the path decides.
The redirection after a closing } or ) is judged on that closing command, not on the group: equivalent for the write rules.
